record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: For a three-dimensional Robertson-Walker brane coupled to a scalar field in a five-dimensional bulk, do regular asymptotic solutions exist, and if so can they support the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant while accounting for the role of curvature and the comparison with the Minkowski-brane case?

evidence.quote:
4.1 RW branes and scalar ﬁelds
The singularity structure and the corresponding asymptotic behavior of a 3D RW brane coupled to a scalar ﬁeld in a ﬁve-dimensional bulk can be analyzed in full generality using the method of asymptotic splittings. One central issue is to examine the existence of regular solutions, and in accordance with the self-tuning proposal, to address the cosmological constant problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3-dimensional Robertson–Walker brane embedded in a 5-dimensional bulk spacetime, coupled to a bulk scalar field φ. The brane metric is of FRW form with scale factor a(t) and spatial curvature k ∈ {−1, 0, +1}, and the bulk Einstein equations are sourced by the scalar field together with brane stress-energy.

(a) Using the method of asymptotic splittings (i.e., decomposing the vector field of the dynamical system governing a(t), φ(t) and the bulk warp factor into dominant balances and subdominant tails, and analyzing Fuchsian/Kovalevskaya exponents), classify all possible asymptotic behaviors of the solutions near finite-time or infinite-time limits.

(b) Determine whether there exist asymptotic solutions that are regular (free of finite-distance singularities in the metric and scalar field) for the curved cases k = ±1 as well as for k = 0.

(c) For those regular families (when they exist), decide whether they realize the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant: namely, whether a flat (or de Sitter–like with tunable curvature) induced 4-dimensional geometry can be obtained on the brane without fine-tuning of the brane tension / vacuum energy.

(d) Compare these results with the analogous classification for a flat Minkowski brane coupled to the same bulk scalar, and identify the role played by the spatial curvature k of the brane.
artifact.status_search_result: The self-tuning problem for the cosmological constant on branes in 5D bulk with a scalar field has been studied in many setups (e.g., holographic self-tuning, P(X,φ) models, bulk black hole configurations), with partial successes for flat Minkowski branes but persistent obstructions (hidden fine-tunings, singularities) in the general case. For curved Robertson–Walker branes analyzed via asymptotic splittings, no complete classification establishing regular self-tuning solutions appears in the literature; the problem is generally regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: Self-tuning of the cosmological constant in brane-worlds with P(X,φ)
status_evidence.snippet: Models requiring that the 4d curvature of the maximally symmetric 3-brane world-volume vanishes independently of the 4d effective vacuum energy.
status_evidence.claim: Self-tuning remains an active area with ongoing constructions and obstructions.

status_evidence.title: Brane cosmology and the self-tuning of the cosmological constant in the presence of bulk black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmology of brane-worlds embedded in a higher-dimensional bulk black hole geometry, motivated by the holographic self-tuning proposal.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to probe whether brane configurations can realize self-tuning, indicating the problem is not settled for curved RW branes.

status_evidence.title: Holographic self-tuning of the cosmological constant
status_evidence.snippet: Holographic mechanism proposed for self-tuning in 5D bulk-scalar setups.
status_evidence.claim: Different proposals exist but a complete resolution for RW branes via asymptotic analysis is not established.
